as valid. `Indices_Calculation_Steps_IBTS` [@ices2022ibtsindices] contains no occurrence of `SpecVal` ([D16](#d16))
at all. A rule stated for one survey and absent for another is not a rule of
the format.

**Can-Mar is the exception that breaks the usual filter.** It puts real
`LngtClass`/`HLNoAtLngt` data on `"5"` rows, where every other survey uses
`"5"` for a length-free presence marker. Filtering to `"1"` there discards
genuine length data. Treat Can-Mar separately.

## 6. Haul duration and hourly rates {#haul-duration-and-hourly-rates}

An hourly rate needs a duration. 217 hauls report `HaulDuration == 0` — 200 of
them `DataType` C, 11 R and 6 P — and 2 report a negative value (both Can-Mar
2017, `-514` and `-238`, already flagged `HaulValidity` `"I"`). A further **51
hauls carry no duration at all**, which is a third case: it is not caught by a
`HaulDuration <= 0` test at all, and reaches the same `NA` only because a
missing value propagates. All three together, 270 hauls:

```{r}
dr_con("HH") |>
  filter(is.na(HaulDuration) | HaulDuration <= 0) |>
  count(DataType, HaulDuration)
```

```
  DataType HaulDuration   n
         C            0 200
         R            0  11
         P            0   6
         R         -514   1
         R         -238   1
         C           NA  33
         R           NA  18
```

No ICES document states anything about a zero, negative or absent haul
duration. `{obus}`'s treatment is a defensible choice in a documented silence, and the rule
is `{obus}`'s own, not ICES's: **where the duration is not positive, any figure
that needs it is `NA`.**

The direction depends on `DataType`, because `C` reports a rate and derives
the haul total, while everything else reports the haul total and derives the
rate:

| | non-`C` | `C` |
|---|---|---|
| hourly rate (`n_hour`, `n_totalnumber_hour`, `w_hour`) | derived — `NA` | reported — kept |
| per-haul total (`n_haul`, `n_totalnumber`, `w_haul`) | reported — kept | derived — `NA` |

Without this the arithmetic produces `Inf` on one side and a plausible-looking
`0` on the other. The `0` is the worse of the two: it looks like a real
observation.

**A documented note of caution.** The 2006 ICES workshop report on variance
estimation — circulated in draft, and marked `DRAFT` on its own cover — carries
an unresolved editorial query in its body text, beside a CPUE formula with no
duration term at all:

> [Are they assuming each haul is one hour? If not should number of hours
> fished be included in the division?]

([D13](#d13).)

Its 2007 successor **deleted the question and kept the formula**. ICES's own
authors were not certain whether duration belongs in the divisor.

## 7. Which hauls count {#which-hauls-count}

`haulval` is an argument of both `dr_HL_length()` and `dr_HL_summary()`; it
takes the `HaulValidity` codes to keep, and `NULL` keeps every haul. What is
there to choose from:

```{r}
dr_con("HH") |> count(HaulValidity)
```

```
  HaulValidity      n
             V 144713
             I   3468
             N    868
             A    815
             C    317
             M     36
```
 The filter is applied to HH before the join, in
`.dr_hh_cols_for_hl()`, so both tables stay in lockstep on which hauls are in
scope.

The only ICES statement of which codes count is survey-specific:
`Indices_Calculation_Steps_BITS` restricts to *"hauls with validity codes 'V'
and 'N'"*. The IBTS procedure states none. `{obus}` does not pick a default.

## 8. Missing values, and what `-9` means {#missing-values-and-what--9-means}

The `General Notes` sheet instructs submitters:

> For the fields with no information but header, please submit -9

So the format has no concept of "blank" — an absent value is submitted as
`-9`. That is more useful than a bare null, because where a field has a
vocabulary ICES gives `-9` a meaning specific to that field, and the meanings
are not all the same kind of thing:

| Field | Meaning of `-9` |
|---|---|
| `Sex` (current: `SpeciesSex`) | "not sampled" — distinct from `U`, "Unidentified" |
| `DevStage` | "No information" |
| `DataType` | "Invalid hauls" — a real classification, not an absence |

**The archive:** zero `-9` values anywhere in HL. `opus` resolves them when
building the archive, nulling any whose vocabulary label means absence and
keeping the three that assert something (`Tickler`, `AgePlusGroup`,
`DataType`). That line — keep a sentinel that states a fact, null one that
states nothing — is why an `NA` `SpeciesSex` in `{obus}` reads as "not sampled".

**`{obus}`:** never re-introduces a sentinel. It cannot tell which `NA`s were
`-9`, and a sentinel placed back into a numeric column would corrupt any sum
taken over it.

**Dummy records.** The FAQ prescribes a placeholder HL record for hauls with
no catch. Its example is

```
HL,1,SCO,SCO3,GOV,60,-9,P,S01,1,2010,W,126417,0,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9,-9
```

24 fields, matching the HL layout, with `SpecVal` = `0` at position 14 — while
the FAQ's own adjacent instruction is to *"report -9 for all other fields"*
([D18](#d18)).
These records are legitimate artefacts and must be excluded before any
reconciliation of counts. (An earlier reading of this record placed the `0` in
the `CatIdentifier` position; it does not fall there, and the FAQ's
`CatIdentifier` rule is untouched by it.)

## Register of cross-document discrepancies

Every entry below was checked by opening the cited file. Where an earlier
reading overstated a discrepancy's severity or genre, the entry says so.

The register is long because ICES publishes a great deal: each entry is a
place where two ICES statements, or one statement and ICES's own data, could
be laid side by side at all. Entries recording something ICES has since
corrected are marked **resolved** and kept rather than deleted, because
documentation and code built against the older wording remain in circulation.
A few entries compare document vintages; they earn their place either because
the archive still holds data submitted under the earlier reading, or because
the way the change was made is itself the observation.

### Discrepancies that change the number you compute

#### D1 — `TotalNo` and `NoMeas` given the same defining formula {#d1}

**Severity:** Contradiction

`TotalNo=SUM(HLNoAtLngt)` (HL row 17) and `NoMeas=Sum(HLNoAtLngt)` (HL row 19) in the same current sheet. Cannot both hold when `SubFactor > 1`. Falsified by the workbook's own Example file (237 against 9766.059).

#### D2 — `HLNoAtLngt` redefined from raised to measured {#d2}

**Severity:** Contradiction, resolved

`HLNoAtLngt` was **already-raised** by definition (`HLNoAtLngt=NoMeas*Subfactor`) until the IBTSWG/WGDG harmonisation redefined it as the raw measured count. The redefinition reverses the field's meaning, and it is the correct reading — the workbook's own Example file contradicted the old definition throughout the time it stood. Kept here because code and documentation built against the old wording remain in circulation. The change is minuted in IBTSWG 2024 §3.3 [@ices2025ibtswg]; the `General Notes` list it only under "Improved descriptions".

#### D3 — Two `TotalNo` formulas two paragraphs apart {#d3}

**Severity:** Contradiction

FAQ p. 18 gives **two different `TotalNo` formulas two paragraphs apart**. Line 745, R: *"TotalNo = Sum (HLNoAtLngt) x SubFactor"*. Line 764, S: *"TotalNo = Sum (HLNoAtLngt)"*, with the `SubFactor` term dropped — even though line 756, in the same S block, says *"Value is always > 1. Make sure that TotalNo = NoMeas x SubFactor"*, and the FAQ's own Example 1 is a `DataType` S case giving 50 → 800. The S block's own worked example falsifies the S block's own formula.

#### D4 — `TotalNo`'s scope was clarified after the data was submitted {#d4}

**Severity:** Contradiction, realised in the data

The current field descriptions and the FAQ agree — `TotalNo` is a total per species × sex × devstage × category — but the descriptions previously read haul × species [@ices2023fielddesc], and submissions follow both conventions. Nothing in the record marks which a row follows, so this one cannot be closed by reading the documents; it is resolved per group, arithmetically ([how `{obus}` resolves a repeated `TotalNo`](#how-obus-deduplicates-totalno)).

#### D5 — The index procedures never reference `TotalNo` {#d5}

**Severity:** Silence, material

The IBTS and BITS **index-calculation procedures never reference `TotalNo` at any step** (zero grep hits in either), while the format publishes it as a non-mandatory field. *Narrowed:* it is **not** true that ICES never consumes `TotalNo`. WKDATR13 (2013) §3.2.1.3 agrees exactly this comparison as submission check 1 of 4 — *"HL Records - Sum(Number at Length) vs. Reported Total Number for each Haul/Species/Sex/Category"*, with a worked 2,473-fish example; the DATSU check register consumes it (*"If validity code is 4 then TotalNo > 0"*); and WKABSENS step 17a uses it as a fallback. What is missing is any statement of what a *user* should do when the two disagree.

#### D6 — `DataType` P has no published raising rule {#d6}

**Severity:** Material silence

`DataType` P has **no raising, `TotalNo`, `SubFactor` or `CatCatchWgt` rule in any published ICES document.** HH row 29 enumerates the code and stops. The FAQ does not contain the word "pseudo". The only guidance is the unpublished 2021 memo.

#### D7 — `DataType` C omits `HLNoAtLngt` from its per-hour rule {#d7}

**Severity:** Material

HH row 29 says only *"C: CPUE (per hour) data; TotalNo and CatCatchWgt are adjusted per hour trawling"* — omitting `HLNoAtLngt`, which HL row 25 and FAQ p. 19 both make per-hour for C. A reader could act on the omission.

#### D8 — `SubFactor`'s stated scope contradicts its own formula {#d8}

**Severity:** Ambiguity

`SubFactor` is described as varying *"by haul, species, sex, length"* (FAQ p. 18) while `TotalNo = NoMeas × SubFactor` presumes one scalar per category. *Downgraded from a contradiction to an ambiguity:* Annex I applies the identical parenthetical to **every** HL field, including `"Total number (TotalNo): subfact*nomeas (by haul, species, sex, category, length)"`, so the list is describing the HL **row key** the field is carried on, not asserting that the value varies. The current `SubFactor` description gives no key list at all. `{obus}`'s per-row product remains the safer implementation, but this is not a documented contradiction.

#### D9 — Units call `HLNoAtLngt` “number of fish” with no C carve-out {#d9}

**Severity:** Material

The units specification asserts `HLNoAtLngt` is *"Number of fish"* **unconditionally**, in both v3.0 and v3.1, with no `DataType` C carve-out anywhere — contradicting the per-hour rule in the format sheet and the FAQ. `TotalNo` and `NoMeas` are likewise flat "Number of fish".

#### D21 — CPUEL gear-standardises cod and nothing else {#d21}

**Severity:** Material

**CPUEL's `CPUE_number_per_hour` is not a homogeneous quantity across species**: cod is gear-standardised, nothing else is, and both sit in the same column with no marker. The BITS conversion table (`ConversionFactor_TVL.csv`, Oeberst 2013 [@ices2014bitsconversion]) contains exactly one species — `Gadus morhua`, all 1,812 rows, across 12 gears — and ICES states an exclusion outright for another (*"For flounder… no conversion factor is applied"*). Measured 2026-09-07 over ~1.1M BITS CPUEL-vs-`{obus}` cells (`data-raw/CHECK_cpuel_multiplier.R`): **61.8%** of 274,821 `Gadus morhua` cells carry a non-unit factor, against **0.2%** for plaice (95,230 cells), 1.6% flounder, 0.8% herring, 0.6% sprat, 0.0% long rough dab — noise everywhere but cod. The exposure is not historical: BITS fishes TVS and TVL **side by side in every year** (plaice 71/29 post-2001, cod 62/38), and TVS→TVL is exactly the conversion cod receives — 1.10 below 25 cm, 1.20 at 25–29 cm, **1.55 at 30 cm and above**, i.e. across the whole commercially relevant range. So two plaice CPUEs from different gears in one file are not comparable, while the same pair for cod has been reconciled. The units specification defines the column as *"Catch in numbers per hour of hauling"* and says nothing further. *Scoped:* the absent plaice factor is not itself the defect — a factor needs paired-gear trials and Oeberst 2013 was a cod study; the defect is publishing corrected and uncorrected values in one undifferentiated column. See D20 for the documentation side.

#### D23 — WKABSENS's raising recipe contradicts ICES's own CPUEL {#d23}

**Severity:** Contradiction, adjudicated

An ICES publication and an ICES product disagree about how to raise `DataType`
`C`, and only the product is right. WKABSENS 2021 [@ices2021wkabsens] (3.3, step 17) gives
*"Multiplier = HaulDur/60 if DataType in ('C'); Multiplier = SubFactor if
DataType in ('S','R')"* — one multiplier or the other. ICES's **CPUEL** product
applies **both**: over 1,721 matched haul × species × length cells on the 36
BITS hauls where the two rules diverge, the median ratio of
`CPUE_number_per_hour` to the two-multiplier figure is exactly 1.000, against
3.000 for the one-multiplier figure. The submissions agree with the product —
across their 113 sub-sampling groups `TotalNo` never equals Σ`HLNoAtLngt`,
equals Σ`HLNoAtLngt` × `SubFactor` in 102, and Σ`HLNoAtLngt` equals `NoMeas` in
108, so `HLNoAtLngt` there is a measured sub-sample and not an hourly rate.
Following WKABSENS understates those records by up to 167.94 times. The
DATRAS R package [@kristensen2023datraspkg] implemented WKABSENS's rule until 2023-04-11, then replaced it
over the note *"some BITS hauls (all LT and some DK) have dataType C but
SubFactor>1 - two multipliers needed!"*, so WKABSENS documents behaviour ICES's
own production has superseded. *Scoped:* the recipe is not wrong in general —
it is correct wherever the format's own `SubFactor = 1` rule for `C` is
honoured, which is everywhere except these 1,832 rows. `{obus}` follows the
product, and flags every affected record `CNT_C_SUBFACTOR_CONFLICT`.
Reproduced by `data-raw/CHECK_cpuel_multiplier.R`; see also [D20](#d20) and
[D21](#d21).

### Discrepancies that change which rows, or which units

#### D10 — `NoMeas` cannot hold its own defining formula {#d10}

**Severity:** Material

`NoMeas` has `MaxWidth 3` (≤ 999) yet is defined as `Sum(HLNoAtLngt)`, where each length row is `MaxWidth 10`. The field cannot hold its own defining formula for any sub-sample of 1,000 or more. A reason not to trust `NoMeas` as an arbiter.

#### D11 — `CatCatchWgt`'s scope includes sex; `{obus}`'s weights do not {#d11}

**Severity:** Material

`SpeciesCategoryWeight`'s key **includes both sex and devstage** in the current descriptions — *"cruise haul, species, sex, devstage and subsampling category identifier"* — while `{obus}` treats a weight repeated across them as one weight. FAQ p. 19 cuts the other way for `DataType` C — *"the total catch weight per species per haul"*, no sex, no category — which is a documentary point in `{obus}`'s favour.

#### D12 — BTS indices standardised to half an hour, caveat dropped {#d12}

**Severity:** Contradiction, realised

BTS indices *"standardised by half an hour haul and not by one hour"* (2006), a caveat dropped from the 2007 successor, while the units specification labels everything "per hour of hauling". *Not latent — realised:* IBTSWG 2025 Table 3.8.1 records CEFAS NS-IBTS Q1 from 1978 submitted per half hour, `TotalNo` "122→244", plus a 100 g unit convention, `CatCatchWgt` "2750→55".

#### D13 — An unresolved editorial query left in the 2006 report {#d13}

**Severity:** Contradiction

The 2006 variance-estimation report [@ices2006wkvarest] carries an **unresolved editorial query in its body text** — *"[Are they assuming each haul is one hour? …]"* — beside a formula with no duration term; the 2007 successor deleted the question and kept the formula. *Framing corrected:* the 2006 document is marked `DRAFT` on its own cover, so it is an ICES workshop report circulated in draft, not a published standard.

#### D14 — A raising sentence deleted between 2006 and 2007 {#d14}

**Severity:** Maintenance

*"the length distribution is raised up with the total catch in number"* (2006, BITS herring and sprat), **deleted** from the 2007 successor with no note. *Downgraded:* this sits in a survey-description section reporting BITS national practice, not in a specification, and it does not in fact conflict with the exchange mechanism — a provider who raises a length distribution to a known total would report the derived ratio as `SubFactor`. Keep the silent deletion as a maintenance-quality observation; drop the claim of a contradictory raising rule.

#### D15 — “We disregard the issue of sub-sampling the catch by length” {#d15}

**Severity:** Material silence, narrowed

*"We disregard the issue of sub-sampling the catch by length"* (2006, §5). *Corrected:* the companion 2007 quotation *"This parameter is ignored in this analysis"* is **not** about sub-sampling — it concerns the number of fish measured as a driver of index accuracy in a sampling-intensity simulation, scoped explicitly to "this analysis". Neither document is a format standard. The inference that this is *why* no rounding or reconciliation rule was ever written is a **hypothesis**, and D5's own counter-evidence (WKDATR13, 2013) shows ICES did take the reconciliation question up.

#### D16 — `SpecVal` rules stated per survey, or not at all {#d16}

**Severity:** Material

IBTS states no `SpecVal` rule at all; BITS specifies `SpecValCode = 1 OR NULL` and treats missing as valid. Survey-specific in the documentation.

#### D17 — `LngtClass` mixes units within one column {#d17}

**Severity:** Material

`LngtClass` carries **mixed units within one column**, and the format standard's `Vocab` column is populated in exactly one cell across all three unaggregated sheets. The self-described format standard never enumerates its own code values.

#### D18 — The dummy HL record contradicts its own instruction {#d18}

**Severity:** Material, narrowed

The FAQ-mandated dummy HL record carries `SpecVal = 0` while the FAQ's own adjacent instruction is to *"report -9 for all other fields"*. These records are legitimate artefacts and must be excluded before any reconciliation. *Corrected:* the `0` falls in the `SpecVal` position, not `CatIdentifier`; the FAQ's *"cannot be reported as 0"* `CatIdentifier` rule is untouched by it, and `-9` in the remaining fields is what the `General Notes` require.

#### D19 — Units v3.1 renames three fields with an empty version note {#d19}

**Severity:** Material

Units v3.1 (18-06-2021) renames **three** fields (`GearExp`→`GearEx`, `Stratum`→`DepthStratum`, `BycSpecRecCode`→`BySpecRecCode`), **deletes the `Survey` row** from the Exchange table, gives `Country` two different vocabulary refs in one document (`ref=4` and `ref=337`), and drops two whole products — all with an **empty version note**. `CANoAtLngt` carries two incompatible units ("Number of fish" / "Catch in numbers per hour"); `Age_n` has three across products. *Corrected:* an earlier count of four renames included `Bootnumber`, which disappears with the dropped Bootstrap product, and `MaturityScale`, which is newly added.

#### D20 — BITS gear-conversion scope stated three ways {#d20}

**Severity:** Contradiction, adjudicated

BITS gear-conversion scope stated three ways in one document: cod only (*"In case of cod (Gadus morhua), conversion factors are used…"*); unconditional (*"CPUE are converted to standard trawl by multiplying with a conversion factor"*); and *"apply fishing power"*, a term that occurs twice and is never defined. *Adjudicated 2026-09-07 against ICES's own CPUEL product* (`data-raw/CHECK_cpuel_multiplier.R`): **the cod-only reading is the operative one**, and cleanly so. Over 1,721 CPUEL-vs-`{obus}` cells on 36 BITS hauls, all 839 `Gadus morhua` cells carry a non-unit factor and every other species — herring, sprat, flounder, on the same hauls and the same gear — is exactly 1.00; of 840 non-unit cells 839 are cod. The factor is a step function of length, as Annex 3's gear × species × length-class table is shaped: 1.10 at 5–24 cm (130 cells), 1.20 at 25–29 cm (132), 1.55 at 30–90 cm (577). The document remains self-contradictory; what is settled is which reading ICES implements. Note the corollary — **CPUEL is not a pure raising of HL**, so any cell-level comparison against it must expect this factor. The consequence for every *other* BITS species, which receives no conversion at all while sharing the column and the units, is D21.

#### D22 — CPUEL does not preserve the submitted length grid {#d22}

**Severity:** Material, scoped

**CPUEL does not preserve the submitted length grid, and is inconsistent about it.** The units specification defines its `LngtClass` as *"In millimetres"* and says nothing further, but millimetre-resolution submissions are silently floored and merged into whole centimetres for part of the archive. Worked example (`BITS:2010:1:LT:LTDA:TVS:26052:7`, *Osmerus eperlanus*, `LengthCode` `0`): the submission is three classes at 95, 180 and 185 mm, one fish each; `{obus}` publishes 95→2, 180→2, 185→2 per hour and CPUEL publishes 90→2, 180→**4**, having floored 95→90 and merged 185 into 180. Measured over BITS 2026-09-07, **15,235** `{obus}` cells have no CPUEL partner at their exact length under the millimetre codes — `0`: 13,074, 64.2% of them sub-centimetre; `.`: 2,161, 100% sub-centimetre. **Totals are preserved** (both sides give 6 smelt per hour in the example), so this changes the *distribution*, not the catch — which makes it invisible to any check that sums over length, and material to every length spectrum, mean length or ALK input taken from CPUEL. *Scoped, twice:* no rule is characterised, because CPUEL retains sub-centimetre resolution 48.8% of the time under `LengthCode` `0` rather than flooring uniformly; and this is **not** the driver of CPUEL-vs-`{obus}` cell disagreement, whose worst group is `LengthCode` `1` (centimetres, 75.6% agreement over 510,933 cells) where binning cannot apply — that residual is D21's gear conversion plus CPUEL's batch vintage. Both the worked example and every figure above are checks in `data-raw/CHECK_cpuel_multiplier.R` §6, including the two scoping clauses.

### Minor discrepancies, and what they say about maintenance

- The December 2024 New Headers Lookup gives `RecordHeader` as its own old name in all four sheets; `getDatrasFieldList` gives `RecordType` → `RecordHeader` for HH, HL, CA and LT, and `RecordType` is what the exchange file carries.
- Annex I indexes `TotalNo` *"(by haul, species, sex, category, length)"* — by length, which is impossible for a category total.
- The Example file's `TotalNo = 9766.059` carries three decimals against its own declared `decimal2` type.
- The current `General Notes` claim *"Decimal data types reduced to only one type"*, while the same workbook's sheets still carry `decimal1`, `decimal2` and `decimal4`.
- `Survey` went from `Mandatory` blank to `Mandatory = Yes` in all three unaggregated sheets with no version note.
- The `-9` rule was narrowed to *"fields with no information but header"* without announcement.
- The two upload guides disagree: *"A valid file should contain 3 record types"* against *"A valid file should contain at least 2 record types"*.
- `Indices_Calculation_Steps_IBTS` section II step (a) is textually garbled in the published PDF.
- `Indices_Calculation_Steps_BITS` Annex 6 duplicates its five Quarter-1 lookup rows verbatim after the Quarter-4 block.
- The 2006 variance-estimation report contains `Error! Bookmark not defined.` as body text.

## An engineering note: R and SQL disagree about `NA`

Not a DATRAS matter, but the single largest source of silent defects in this
code. `{obus}` runs the same functions eagerly (data frames, in the tests) and
lazily (DuckDB, in the build), and the two backends differ in four ways.
Anyone extending these functions needs all four.

**1. Joining.** SQL treats `NULL = NULL` as unknown, so a lazy join drops
every row with an `NA` key — and `SpeciesSex` is `NA` in 54% of HL, with
`SpeciesCategory`, `SpeciesValidity` and `TotalNumber` able to be `NA` too.
Every join in `dr_HL_summary()` whose key can hold `NA` carries
`na_matches = "na"`, which dbplyr renders as `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` and DuckDB
supports natively. Without it, every `NA`-sex row fails to find its own
length-derived expectation, never reconciles, falls to the fallback, and
undercounts. Confirmed on a real case
(`BITS:1999:1:DK:26HI:TVS:017492:22`, aphia 127143): true total 4, and 3
without the flag.

**2. Aggregating over an all-`NA` group.** `sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)` is `0` in R
and `NULL` in SQL. Every aggregation here carries an explicit non-`NA` counter
(`.n_ok`, `.h_ok`, `.w_ok`, `.wh_ok`) and forces `NA` when the counter is
zero, so both backends agree. Without it the eager path silently converts a
deliberate `NA` — a missing `SubsamplingFactor`, a non-positive
`HaulDuration`, a species that was never weighed — straight back into the
confident `0` it was meant to prevent.

**3. Self-reference inside `summarise()`.** dplyr evaluates expressions in
order, so `n_ok = sum(!is.na(n_haul))` written *after* `n_haul = sum(n_haul)`
sees the new scalar; SQL resolves every aggregate against the source column.
`dr_HL_length()` renames to `.n_raw`/`.h_raw` before aggregating, so the two
agree by construction rather than by luck.

**4. String concatenation with `NA`.** On a plain data frame R's `paste(sep =)`
renders an `NA` field as the literal two-character string `"NA"`; on a
`tbl_lazy`, dbplyr translates the same call to DuckDB's `CONCAT_WS()`, which
drops `NA` fields instead. `.id` is the join key between HH, HL and CA, so it
must come out identical whichever backend built it. `.dr_concat_ws()` builds
the `NA`-skipping behaviour explicitly from `is.na()`, `case_when()` and
`paste0()`, which translate the same way on both — with one deliberate
departure from raw `CONCAT_WS()`: when every field is `NA` it returns `NA`,
not `CONCAT_WS()`'s `""`, because an empty string would collide every such row
onto one `.id`.

Each of these produced a real, silent, wrong number at some point. Keeping
both an eager test suite and a lazy build is what catches them; neither does
alone.
